name: TMC2209 silent stepper motor driver
description: Trinamic (Analog Devices) TMC2209 silent driver for one bipolar stepper motor: STEP/DIR control, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 or 1/64 step selected by MS1/MS2 and interpolated to 1/256, near-silent stealthChop2 by default (spreadCycle, stallGuard4 and coolStep by UART), current set by a trimpot (1.4 A RMS per coil continuous, 2.8 A peak), motor supply 5.5-28 V, logic I/O 3-5 V. EN is pulled up on the board, so the motor only runs when EN is driven low. Sold as: BIGTREETECH TMC2209 V1.2 (StepStick format), 16 pins in two rows: EN MS1 MS2 PDN PDN CLK STEP DIR, opposite side VM GND A2 A1 B1 B2 VDD GND, plus VREF/INDEX/DIAG pads on the top edge.
eli5: Turns a stepper motor one tiny, quiet click every time your board sends it a pulse, in the direction you choose.

pins.name: EN
pins.description: ENN, active low: low = motor outputs on, high = outputs off (shaft free) and DIAG error reset. The BTT V1.2 board pulls it UP to VDD (R1 20 kOhm), so the motor stays off until you drive EN low

pins.name: MS1
pins.description: MS1_AD0 microstep select (internal pull-down). MS2/MS1: 00 = 1/8, 01 = 1/32, 10 = 1/64, 11 = 1/16 step (differs from the TMC2208). Also UART address bit 0

pins.name: MS2
pins.description: MS2_AD1 microstep select (internal pull-down). Also UART address bit 1

pins.name: PDN
pins.description: PDN_UART (factory jumper T1 routes the chip's PDN_UART to this pin; pulled to GND by R5 20 kOhm = automatic standstill current reduction). Single-wire UART for register setup. Leave unconnected in STEP/DIR mode

pins.name: PDN2
pins.description: Second pin printed PDN: only connected to PDN_UART if jumper T1 is moved. Leave unconnected

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: External clock input, pulled to GND on the board (R3 20 kOhm) = internal 12 MHz clock. Leave unconnected

pins.name: STEP
pins.description: STEP: each low-to-high edge moves the motor one microstep. Min 100 ns high and 100 ns low. No pull on the board: never leave floating

pins.name: DIR
pins.description: DIR: direction, read on each STEP rising edge (internal pull-down)

pins.name: VM
pins.description: Motor supply 5.5-28 V (chip VS with its internal 5 V regulator) from a separate supply, not the microcontroller, with a >= 100 uF electrolytic capacitor across VM/GND at the board. The chip's logic and the VREF trimpot also run from VM

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Motor supply ground (printed GND, next to VM); joined to the logic GND on the board

pins.name: B2
pins.description: Motor coil B, second wire (OB2). Connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Logic I/O supply VCC_IO 3.0-5.25 V. Use 3.3 V with a 3.3 V microcontroller (input thresholds scale with VCC_IO)

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Logic ground (printed GND, next to VDD): connect to the microcontroller GND

buildNotes: Two supplies: logic VDD (VCC_IO) 3-5 V from the microcontroller (3.3 V for an ESP32/Pico) and motor VM 5.5-28 V from a separate supply (12 V or 24 V typical). Join the grounds.
The TMC2209's own logic runs from an internal regulator fed by VM: with only VDD connected the chip does nothing.
EN is pulled up to VDD on the BTT V1.2 board (outputs off). Drive it low from a GPIO, or tie it to GND, or the motor never moves.
Put a 100 uF or larger electrolytic capacitor across VM and GND right at the board.
Never connect or disconnect the motor while VM is powered: it destroys the driver.

Set the current with the trimpot (VM must be on to measure it): IRMS = 0.325 V / (Rsense + 0.02 Ohm) / sqrt(2) x VREF / 2.5 V. With the board's 0.11 Ohm sense resistors, IRMS = 0.71 x VREF (factory VREF about 1.2 V -> 0.85 A RMS). Keep it at or below 1.4 A RMS (VREF about 2.0 V) for continuous running.
Microstepping (MS2 MS1): 00 = 1/8 (default, pins open), 01 = 1/32, 10 = 1/64, 11 = 1/16. This differs from the TMC2208 and A4988 tables.
Insert the board the right way round (EN opposite VM). Plugged in backwards it is destroyed when powered.
The chip is cooled through the board: fit the heat sink (not touching any pin) and give it airflow. It shuts down when it overheats.
The VREF, INDEX and DIAG pads on the top edge are optional: DIAG goes high on a driver error or stall (stallGuard, UART setup needed).
sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/makerbase-mks/MKS-StepStick-Driver/master/MKS%20TMC2209/U0000000291%20IC%20TMC2209-LA%20%20QFN28.pdf (TMC2209 datasheet copy used for reading: ratings, timing, AT#1, current formula)
https://github.com/bigtreetech/BIGTREETECH-TMC2209-V1.2 (Schematic/TMC2209-V1.2.pdf; manual/TMC2209-V1.2-manual.pdf pin designation image, MS1/MS2 table, current formula)

driver.code:
# TMC2209 silent stepper motor driver (Trinamic / ADI TMC2209), MicroPython driver, STEP/DIR standalone mode.
# Written from the TMC2209 datasheet and the BIGTREETECH TMC2209 V1.2 schematic and manual.
#   STEP:  each LOW->HIGH edge moves the motor one microstep (DEDGE=0, the power-up default).
#          Min HIGH and min LOW time 100 ns (tSH, tSL). No pull on the board: never leave it floating.
#   DIR:   direction, sampled on the STEP edge. Setup and hold time to STEP: 20 ns (tDSU, tDSH).
#   ENN (board pin EN, active low): high = power stage off, all motor outputs floating; also resets a DIAG error.
#          The BTT V1.2 board pulls EN UP to VCC_IO (VDD) with 20 kOhm (R1), so the motor stays OFF until EN is low.
#   MS1/MS2 (internal pull-downs): MS2 MS1 = 00 -> 1/8, 01 -> 1/32, 10 -> 1/64, 11 -> 1/16 microsteps
#          (NOT the TMC2208 table!), interpolated to 1/256 inside the chip. Left open = 1/8 step
#          (1600 pulses per turn of a 200-step motor). In UART mode the same pins set the UART address.
#   stealthChop2 automatic tuning (AT#1): after the outputs switch on, keep the motor at standstill for
#          up to 130 ms (2^20 + 2*2^18 clocks at 12 MHz) before the first move.
# Logic thresholds scale with VCC_IO (board pin VDD, 3.0-5.25 V): with a 3.3 V microcontroller power VDD from 3.3 V.
# The chip's logic runs from its internal 5 V regulator, fed from VM: nothing moves without the motor supply.
from machine import Pin
import time

# microsteps -> (MS1, MS2), datasheet table "MS1/MS2: configuration of microstep resolution for STEP input"
_MODES = {8: (0, 0), 32: (1, 0), 64: (0, 1), 16: (1, 1)}

_AT1_MS = 130  # stealthChop AT#1 standstill time with the internal 12 MHz clock


class TMC2209:
    def __init__(self, step, dir, en=None, ms=None):
        """step, dir: GPIO numbers wired to STEP and DIR (both required).
        en: GPIO wired to EN. The BTT V1.2 board pulls EN up (outputs off): if you pass None,
            EN must be tied to GND by a wire. Starts disabled (EN high).
        ms: (ms1, ms2) GPIO numbers, or None (1/8 step through the internal pull-downs)."""
        self.step_pin = Pin(step, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.dir_pin = Pin(dir, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.en = Pin(en, Pin.OUT, value=1) if en is not None else None
        self.ms = [Pin(p, Pin.OUT, value=0) for p in ms] if ms is not None else None
        self.microsteps = 8
        self.position = 0
        self._on = en is None

    def set_microstep(self, div):
        """div = 8, 16, 32 or 64 microsteps per full step. Needs ms= pins."""
        if self.ms is None:
            raise ValueError('MS1/MS2 not wired: board is fixed at 1/8 step')
        if div not in _MODES:
            raise ValueError('TMC2209 pins select 8, 16, 32 or 64 microsteps')
        for p, b in zip(self.ms, _MODES[div]):
            p.value(b)
        self.microsteps = div

    def enable(self, on=True):
        """EN low = motor outputs on (holds torque). EN high = outputs floating (shaft turns freely)."""
        if self.en is None:
            return
        self.en.value(0 if on else 1)
        if on and not self._on:
            time.sleep_ms(_AT1_MS)  # AT#1: standstill at run current before the first step
        self._on = on

    def disable(self):
        self.enable(False)

    def direction(self, forward):
        """Set DIR (1 = forward). Read by the chip on the next STEP rising edge."""
        self.dir_pin.value(1 if forward else 0)
        time.sleep_us(1)  # >= 20 ns setup before STEP

    def step(self, n, delay_us=500):
        """Send n microstep pulses; n < 0 runs backwards. delay_us = time per microstep (>= 2)."""
        if n == 0:
            return
        self.direction(n > 0)
        half = max(1, delay_us // 2)
        s = self.step_pin
        for _ in range(abs(n)):
            s.value(1)
            time.sleep_us(half)   # tSH >= 100 ns
            s.value(0)
            time.sleep_us(half)   # tSL >= 100 ns
        self.position += n

    def steps_per_rev(self, full_steps=200):
        """Microstep pulses for one shaft turn (200 full steps for a 1.8 degree motor)."""
        return full_steps * self.microsteps


def irms_from_vref(vref, rsense=0.11):
    """Standalone RMS coil current (A) set by the VREF trimpot voltage (datasheet):
    IRMS = 325 mV / (RSENSE + 20 mOhm) x 1/sqrt(2) x VREF / 2.5 V.
    The BTT TMC2209 V1.2 uses RSENSE = 0.11 Ohm (R2, R4)."""
    return 0.325 / (rsense + 0.02) / 1.41421356 * vref / 2.5


def vref_for_current(irms, rsense=0.11):
    """VREF (volts, measured between the trimpot and GND with VM powered) for an RMS coil current."""
    v = irms * 2.5 * 1.41421356 * (rsense + 0.02) / 0.325
    if v > 2.5:
        raise ValueError('needs VREF > 2.5 V: current too high for this sense resistor')
    return v

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from tmc2209 import TMC2209

# STEP/DIR/EN to GPIOs. MS1/MS2 left open = 1/8 step, so 1600 pulses turn a 200-step motor once.
motor = TMC2209({STEP}, {DIR}, en={EN})
while True:
    motor.enable()            # EN low: outputs on
    motor.step(800)           # half a turn forward
    print('moved 800 steps forward')
    time.sleep(0.5)
    motor.step(-800)
    print('moved 800 steps back')
    motor.disable()           # EN high: outputs off, shaft free
    print('outputs off')
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Drives EN low, steps 800 forward (DIR high) and 800 back (DIR low), then EN high
